content.text: I’ve narrowed the second finding to a product bug, not a README wording problem: several `--head` paths still decorate committed graph data with source read from disk. I’m finishing the implementation boundary now, then I’ll give you one concrete before/after proposal for approval—no edits yet.

The key design choice is now clear: `--head` should read source by the snapshot’s immutable tree ID, not by the moving `HEAD` ref. That keeps snippets, call sites, and symbol bodies aligned with the exact graph snapshot even if the branch moves during a command. I’m checking the regression-test surface before proposing it.

The test boundary is also smaller than the original finding suggested: `search --head` already reads committed content correctly. The remaining functional fixes are `neighbors`, `impact`, and `def`, plus the incorrect `explain --head` provenance label. I won’t broaden this into a search rewrite.

### Finding 2 — High: `--head` mixes source provenance

`neighbors`, `impact`, and text/agent `def` load committed graph data but then read snippets or call sites from the live working tree. `explain --head` also incorrectly labels its results as coming from the working tree. `search --head` is already correct.

Proposed solution:

- Add one snapshot-bound source reader:
  - Default/worktree mode reads from disk.
  - `--head` reads from the exact immutable commit recorded in the snapshot using a single batched Git reader.
- Use it for all source enrichment in `neighbors`, `impact`, and `def`, including ambiguous-match bodies and call-site annotations.
- Leave `search` unchanged, adding only a regression test.
- Make the `explain` provenance header mode-aware.
- Add dirty-worktree tests proving every command shows committed content under `--head` and dirty content by default.

Behavior before:

```text
Committed graph entities and edges
        +
dirty working-tree snippets, guards, bodies, or line numbers
```

Behavior after:

```text
--head     → committed graph + committed source
default    → working-tree graph + working-tree source
```

The only user-facing text change would be in `explain`.

Before, in every mode:

```text
DECLARATIONS THE BUILD ERROR NAMED (from the working tree, so your own edits are included)
```

After, in default/worktree mode:

```text
DECLARATIONS THE BUILD ERROR NAMED (from the working tree, so your own edits are included)
```

After, with `--head`:

```text
DECLARATIONS THE BUILD ERROR NAMED (from committed HEAD, so working-tree edits are excluded)
```

I would not change `docs/readme-plan.md` for this finding—the implementation should satisfy its promised tree semantics.

content.text:
### Finding 3 — High: duplicate Claude instruction loading

The repository currently reproduces it:

- [CLAUDE.md](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/CLAUDE.md:1) imports `AGENTS.md`.
- [AGENTS.md](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/AGENTS.md:206) imports the Entire Graph guide.
- `CLAUDE.md` also imports that guide directly.

Claude’s official documentation recommends importing `AGENTS.md` specifically to share instructions without duplication. [Claude Code memory documentation](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory)

Proposed product fix:

- Keep the normal guide pointer in `AGENTS.md`.
- When `init-agents` detects that `CLAUDE.md` directly imports the root `AGENTS.md`, replace its managed direct pointer with a marker-only inheritance notice.
- Otherwise retain the current direct guide pointer in `CLAUDE.md`.
- On later runs, restore the direct pointer if the user removes the `AGENTS.md` import.
- Preserve all unmanaged content and test legacy migration plus byte-for-byte idempotence.

Generated `CLAUDE.md` block before:

```md
<!-- entire-graph:begin -->
This repo has the entire-graph code graph installed. Before exploring code with
grep/find/whole-file reads, read .entire/graph-agent.md — resolution-first guidance
for using graph retrieval, focused source inspection, and verification.
@.entire/graph-agent.md
<!-- entire-graph:end -->
```

After, when `CLAUDE.md` already imports `AGENTS.md`:

```md
<!-- entire-graph:begin -->
<!-- Entire Graph instructions are inherited through AGENTS.md. -->
<!-- entire-graph:end -->
```

The acceptance criterion stays unchanged; the product will satisfy it. Only the now-stale explanatory paragraph in the plan changes.

Before:

> Test the Claude Code layout where `CLAUDE.md` already imports `AGENTS.md`. `init-agents` writes the same pointer block to both files, so that layout can import the guide twice; document the supported resolution rather than hiding it.

After:

> Test the Claude Code layout where `CLAUDE.md` already imports `AGENTS.md`. `init-agents` must use the existing import as the single path to the Entire Graph guide, migrate legacy duplicate blocks, preserve unrelated content, and remain idempotent on reruns.

If approved, I’ll implement this in another separate product PR.
Ask Claude Claude if it agrees.

I’ll ask the installed Claude Code directly, giving it the current `init-agents` behavior, the proposed marker-only inheritance design, and the edge cases we identified. I’ll return its judgment verbatim enough to preserve the substance, then note where I agree or disagree.

Claude Opus 5 gave a qualified yes:

> “The design principle is right … but steps 2–3 buy a small, possibly zero win with a permanent heuristic parser.”

Its strongest objection is that we have not proven Claude actually loads the guide twice. Claude Code may deduplicate recursive imports by resolved path. It recommends measuring the assembled instruction context first.

If duplication is real, it says the fix must also:

- Ignore the managed block when detecting imports.
- Handle `CLAUDE.md` symlinked to `AGENTS.md`.

Finding 3 is fixed and committed as `97bfc3a`. The branch is clean; generated files are byte-idempotent and the focused test passed.

### Finding 4 — Medium: activation side effects are under-disclosed

Merged code overwrites `.entire/graph-agent.md` completely on every run. It also assumes managed markers are well formed; malformed or duplicate markers can cause repeated appends or overly broad replacement, after the guide has already been written.

I recommend a separate product PR that:

- Validates both instruction files before writing anything.
- Accepts zero markers or exactly one ordered marker pair.
- Refuses malformed, reversed, or duplicate markers without changing any file.
- Reports an actionable recovery error.
- Keeps full replacement of the generated guide intentional.

Then change [docs/readme-plan.md](/Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/docs/readme-plan.md:128) as follows.

Before:

```md
- State that activation is per repository. Before the command, disclose that it:
  - writes `.entire/graph-agent.md`;
  - creates or updates marker-delimited sections in `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`;
  - replaces an existing marker-delimited block in each file on later runs rather
    than appending a second block in that file.
```

After:

```md
- State that activation is per repository. Before the command, disclose that it:
  - creates `.entire/graph-agent.md`, or replaces that generated file in full on
    every rerun, so manual edits there are not preserved;
  - creates `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` if absent, or replaces one intact
    marker-delimited managed block while preserving text outside it;
  - validates both instruction files before writing and refuses malformed,
    reversed, or duplicate Entire Graph markers without changing any file.
```

Before:

```md
- Document removal or reversal only if a supported procedure exists; do not invent one.
```

After:

```md
- In `docs/agents.md`, document recovery from a marker-validation error: back up
  `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`, preserve user-owned text, reduce each file to zero
  or one complete Entire Graph marker pair, and rerun `init-agents`.
  Document ordinary removal or reversal only if a supported procedure exists.
```

I’d also add this acceptance criterion:

```md
- [ ] `init-agents` fails without writes on malformed, reversed, or duplicate
  managed markers, and `docs/agents.md` gives the supported recovery procedure.
```

Approve this solution?
Yes

I’m using the `github:yeet` workflow because the approved fix belongs in another isolated product branch and draft PR. I’ll implement atomic preflight validation first, then update the README-plan branch only after the product behavior is published.

### Ordering

1. Parse flags and validate the repository root.
2. Preflight `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md`.
3. Compute both resulting instruction-file byte slices in memory.
4. Only then create `.entire`, write the guide, write `AGENTS.md`, and—if distinct—write `CLAUDE.md`.
5. Print success lines only after their corresponding writes.

Preflight should:

- `Lstat` both names to distinguish a truly absent path from a dangling symlink.
- Follow existing symlinks with `Stat`.
- Reject dangling symlinks and non-regular targets before any write.
- Use `os.SameFile` on followed metadata.
- For same-inode aliases, read and validate once and return `claude == nil`.

- Optionally collect distinct-file failures with `errors.Join`, so two malformed files can be repaired together.

- `0` begin and `0` end markers.
- `1` begin and `1` end marker, with begin’s byte offset before end’s.

- Begin only.
- End only.

- Duplicate begin.

  body: `## Summary

- inspect and validate both \`AGENTS.md\` and \`CLAUDE.md\` before creating or modifying any activation file
- accept only no Entire Graph markers or exactly one correctly ordered managed-marker pair
- reject malformed, reversed, or duplicate markers with a path-specific recovery error and no writes or success output
- render from the validated snapshots while preserving existing symlink/hard-link behavior, including first-run dangling aliases

## Why

\`init-agents\` previously overwrote \`.entire/graph-agent.md\` before inspecting either instruction file. Its block upsert then used the first raw opening and closing markers without validating their count or order. Malformed or duplicate markers could therefore append more blocks or replace an unexpectedly broad range after another activation file had already changed.

This patch makes marker/read preflight failures non-mutating. Successful activation still intentionally replaces the generated guide in full and preserves user-owned text outside one valid managed block.

- \`mise exec -- go test ./internal/cli\`
- \`mise exec -- go test ./internal/cli -run '^TestCompactNDJSONRejectsTargetedRelationFilters$'\`
- \`mise run check\`
- two independent focused reviews: clean

### Finding 7 — Medium: ADR supersession mechanics are incomplete

ADR 0002 still says working-tree search snapshots are never cached. Current behavior safely caches eligible working-tree snapshots, while the separate provider-record cache remains committed-tree-only.

Therefore ADR 0002 should be partially—not wholly—superseded. Its committed-tree key decision remains valid.

```md
| `docs/adr/0003-working-tree-search-snapshot-cache.md` | Create as Accepted; declare that it partially supersedes ADR 0002 | Working-tree search-snapshot eligibility and isolation; provider-record caching remains committed-tree-only |
```


After:

```md
  `Status: Accepted` and reciprocal metadata that partially supersedes ADR 0002
  only for working-tree search-snapshot eligibility. Document the separate
  working-tree cache identity and provenance; bypass for dirty supported-extension,
  extensionless, or resolver-manifest paths; continued eligibility for other
  known-unsupported-extension paths; `.graphignore` keying; no-HEAD behavior; and
  the continued working-tree bypass in the provider-record cache. Add the
  reciprocal notice to ADR 0002, update `docs/README.md` to scope each ADR's
  authority, and correct the stale `LoadOrBuildProviderSnapshot` source comment.
```

**3. Non-goal boundary**

Before:

```md
- Rewriting historical ADRs, archived plans, or immutable benchmark evidence. A
  new superseding cache ADR is in scope because current behavior has changed.
```

After:

```md
- Rewriting historical ADR decision bodies, archived plans, or immutable
  benchmark evidence. Adding ADR 0003 and updating ADR 0002's supersession
  metadata are in scope because current behavior has changed.
```

**4. Add an acceptance criterion**

```md
- [ ] ADR 0002 and ADR 0003 link to each other, and `docs/README.md` identifies
  ADR 0002 as authoritative for committed-tree cache identity and ADR 0003 as
  authoritative for working-tree search-snapshot eligibility.
```

The intended ADR metadata would be:

```md
# ADR 0002
Status: Accepted
Partially superseded by: [ADR 0003](0003-working-tree-search-snapshot-cache.md) for working-tree search-snapshot eligibility only.

# ADR 0003
Status: Accepted
Partially supersedes: [ADR 0002](0002-committed-tree-cache-key.md) for working-tree search-snapshot eligibility only.
```

```go

```

to:

```go
// Eligible worktree snapshots use a separate namespace; a missing HEAD or a
// dirty supported-extension, extensionless, or resolver-manifest path makes the
// request bypass cache reuse.
```

*** Add File: /Users/thomi/Projects/entire-graph/README.md
+# Entire Graph
+
+Entire Graph is a local static-analysis plugin for the Entire CLI that helps
+coding agents find definitions, relationships, and change impact in Git
+repositories.
+
+Its built-in analyzer parses repository contents with tree-sitter and returns
+ranked source locations, symbols, and static relationships. Analysis runs
+without network egress, hosted model calls, or API keys.
+
+The recommended path is: [install](#install) → [activate it for an
+agent](#activate-it-for-your-coding-agent) → [ask a repository
+question](#try-a-repository-question) → inspect the cited source.
+
+## Install
+
+Entire Graph is an external command for Entire CLI 0.10.0 or later. Install
+`entire` and make sure it is on `PATH`. For macOS and Linux, the common path is:
+
+```sh
+curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
+entire version
+```
+
+See the [Entire CLI installation documentation](https://docs.entire.io/installation)
+for other methods and platforms. `entire enable` configures Entire session
+capture; it is not required to run Entire Graph.
+
+Install the indexed plugin and verify that the command dispatches:
+
+```sh
+entire plugin install graph
+entire graph version
+```
+
+## Activate it for your coding agent
+
+Activation is per repository. Before running it, know that `init-agents`:
+
+- Creates `.entire/graph-agent.md`, or replaces that generated file in full on
+  every successful rerun. Manual edits to it are not preserved.
+- Creates `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` when absent. In existing files it appends
+  one managed block when no Entire Graph markers exist, or replaces exactly one
+  ordered managed block while preserving text outside it.
+- Validates both instruction files before writing. Malformed, reversed, or
+  duplicate Entire Graph markers, and instruction-file targets that are not
+  regular files, stop activation without changing any activation file.
+
+From the repository root, run:
+
+```sh
+entire graph init-agents --repo .
+```
+
+Review `.entire/graph-agent.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and `CLAUDE.md`. Commit them
+together when the instructions should apply to the team. Until these indexable
+Markdown files are committed or otherwise clean, default working-tree queries
+bypass snapshot reuse for the repository.
+
+The generated instructions tell an agent to search the graph before broad code
+exploration, inspect focused source, check related sites when needed, and verify
+its result. You can inspect the guide without writing files:
+
+```sh
+entire graph agent-guide
+```
+
+Instruction discovery differs between coding clients. After activation, start a
+fresh task or session rooted at the repository in a client that reads the
+generated repository instructions.
+
+## Try a repository question
+
+Ask about code in the repository rather than invoking a graph command yourself:
+
+```text
+Without changing repository source files, find where <known feature> is
+implemented, identify what calls it or what changing it would affect, and cite
+the relevant source.
+```
+
+Use the client's visible activity or tool log to verify the workflow:
+
+1. The fresh task discovers the repository instructions.
+2. The agent runs `entire graph search` before broad repository scanning.
+3. It opens focused source around the ranked result.
+4. It uses `neighbors` or `impact` when the relationship or blast radius matters.
+5. Its answer cites the source it checked. For a code change, it also runs the
+   narrowest relevant verification it can identify.
+
+The exact commands and results depend on the repository, so this README does not
+substitute a hand-written transcript for the client activity you can inspect.
+The source task above is read-only, but a graph query may still write a
+derivative local cache.
+
+## Common tasks and cache behavior
+
+Prompts are the primary interface. The graph operation is what the agent uses
+internally, or what you can run directly for debugging and automation.
+
+| Goal | Ask the agent | Graph operation |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Find code for a task | “Find where … is implemented.” | `search` |
+| Understand one definition | “Show and explain the definition of …” | `def` |
+| Inspect callers and relations | “What calls …?” | `neighbors` |
+| Estimate a symbol's blast radius | “What would changing … affect?” | `impact` |
+| Review a commit or branch | “Summarize the semantic changes in …” | `commit` / `diff` |
+| Export the graph | “Export the graph for …” | `snapshot` |
+
+`search`, `def`, `explain`, `neighbors`, and `impact` read the working tree by
+default, so an agent sees current edits. Use `--head` only when the question is
+intentionally about committed state. Whole-graph streams and ref-based analysis
+have command-specific tree semantics; check `entire graph <command> --help`.
+
+Working-tree snapshot reuse is conservative and repository-wide. A dirty path
+with a supported extension, an extensionless path that could be a shebang
+script, or a root manifest used for import resolution bypasses reuse for that
+query. Other dirty, non-manifest paths with known unsupported extensions remain
+eligible. `.graphignore` content is part of the cache key, and a changed
+committed tree selects a different entry.
+
+JSON search output exposes `index_cache_hit`; `--format agent` includes a compact
+cache header. Text output does not report cache state. Caches are derivative
+local state and can be removed and rebuilt.
+
+`entire graph index` warms one committed-tree cache variant, not the default
+working-tree agent path. A later `--head` query reuses it only with the same
+resolved cache directory, profile, ordered ignore/include inputs and their
+contents, and unchanged `.graphignore`. `index` defaults to profile `full`, while
+`search` defaults to `fast`, so their defaults do not share a variant.
+
+## Agent flow, boundaries, and limits
+
+```text
+user prompt → coding agent → repository instructions → entire graph CLI
+            → ranked graph evidence → focused source/test check → sourced answer
+```
+
+- Built-in analysis is local and no-egress; installation obtains software over
+  the network.
+- `init-agents` writes the three disclosed repository instruction files, and
+  queries may write derivative caches.
+- Static relations and dependent counts are not compiler-accurate. Dynamic
+  dispatch, reflection, generated code, runtime wiring, routes, tools, and
+  renames can be heuristic or incomplete.
+- Unsupported languages are inventory-only or produce explicit partial
+  failures. Check support before relying on semantic relations.
+- Working-tree and committed-tree defaults differ by command family.
+- Entire Graph is a one-shot CLI and semantic provider. [Entire Brain is a
+  separate durable consumer and MCP surface](docs/brain-and-graph-boundaries.md);
+  Entire Graph is not a daemon, watcher, hosted memory service, or MCP server.
+
+Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle: inspect the relevant source and
+verify changes with the repository's own tests or build.
+
+## Documentation and manual use
+
+- [Documentation map](docs/README.md) — current references and sources of truth
+- [Language support](docs/language-support.md) — semantic and inventory-only
+  languages
+- [Provider requirements](docs/semantic-provider-requirements.md) — schema,
+  relations, profiles, warnings, and limits
+- [Entire Brain and Entire Graph boundaries](docs/brain-and-graph-boundaries.md)
+- [Benchmark methodology and evidence](docs/benchmarks.md)
+
+For direct inspection, diagnostics, and feature detection:
+
+```sh
+entire graph help
+entire graph capabilities --json
+entire graph doctor --json
+```
+
+For development in this repository:
+
+```sh
+mise run build
+mise run test
+mise run check
+```
+
+Report problems in [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/entireio/entire-graph/issues).
+Entire Graph is distributed under the [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE).
*** End Patch";

+# Entire Graph
+
+Most coding-agent detours happen before the edit, while the agent is still
+trying to find the right code. Entire Graph gives it a local map of the
+repository: ranked source, definitions, callers, types, routes, and change
+impact, all tied back to `file:line` locations it can inspect.
+
+Entire Graph runs as a plugin for the Entire CLI. Its built-in analyzer parses
+the repository with tree-sitter and makes no network requests, model calls, or
+API-key lookups.
+
+## See it work
+
+Here is a real question from this repository:
+
+> Where do we keep terminal escape sequences out of CLI output, and what
+> depends on that code?
+
+The agent searched first, found the implementation, and then checked its blast
+radius. This is an abridged transcript of the graph output:
+
+```text
+search
+1. internal/termsafe/termsafe.go:295-317  appendEscaped
+
+impact
+Impact: appendEscaped (internal/termsafe/termsafe.go:295)
+Blast radius: 34 callers (3 direct, 31 transitive), 1 callee
+
+Direct callers:
+- Writer.Write (internal/termsafe/termsafe.go:83)
+- Line         (internal/termsafe/termsafe.go:112)
+- Bytes        (internal/termsafe/termsafe.go:135)
+```
+
+The agent now has a concrete fix site and a bounded set of related code to
+inspect. On the captured warm-cache run, the `impact` query completed in about
+one second.
+
+## Quick start
+
+Entire Graph requires Entire CLI 0.10.0 or later. Install `entire` and make sure
+it is on `PATH`.
+
+On macOS:
+
+```sh
+brew tap entireio/tap
+brew trust entireio/tap
+brew install --cask entire
+```
+
+On Linux:
+
+```sh
+curl -fsSL https://entire.io/install.sh | bash
+```
+
+For Windows, source builds, and other options, see the [Entire CLI installation
+guide](https://docs.entire.io/installation). Then install the plugin:
+
+```sh
+entire version
+entire plugin install graph
+entire graph version
+```
+
+`entire enable` configures Entire session capture. Entire Graph can run without
+it.
+
+### Add the agent instructions
+
+Activation is per repository. `init-agents` writes
+`.entire/graph-agent.md` and creates or updates a managed block in `AGENTS.md`
+and `CLAUDE.md`. It preserves text outside those blocks. A successful rerun
+replaces the generated guide, so manual edits to that file are not preserved.
+Malformed markers or non-regular instruction-file targets stop activation
+before any of the three files change.
+
+From the repository root, run:
+
+```sh
+entire graph init-agents --repo .
+```
+
+Review the three files and commit them when the instructions should apply to
+the team. Start a fresh agent session in the repository so the client discovers
+the new instructions.
+
+Then ask a normal code question. For example:
+
+> Find where terminal escape sequences are removed from CLI output. Show me
+> what calls that code and which source I should inspect before changing it.
+
+The generated guide asks the agent to use the graph for location, open the
+relevant source, check related sites when they matter, and run focused
+verification after an edit.
+
+## What to ask
+
+Prompts are the main interface. You can also run the commands directly for
+debugging or automation.
+
+| Goal | Example prompt | Graph command |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| Find the implementation | Find where request routing is implemented. | `search` |
+| Read one definition | Show and explain `ResolveRoute`. | `def` |
+| Trace callers or callees | What calls `ResolveRoute`? | `neighbors` |
+| Check the blast radius | What would changing `ResolveRoute` affect? | `impact` |
+| Review a branch | Summarize the semantic changes from `main` to `HEAD`. | `diff` |
+| Export the full graph | Export the repository graph as NDJSON. | `snapshot` |
+
+For a command overview, run `entire graph help`. Use
+`entire graph <command> --help` for its flags and output formats.
+
+## Working tree and cache
+
+Interactive queries such as `search`, `def`, `explain`, `neighbors`, and
+`impact` read the working tree by default, so agents can see uncommitted edits.
+Add `--head` when the question is specifically about committed state.
+
+Queries may write a derivative local cache. `entire graph index` warms one
+committed-tree cache variant for later, matching `--head` queries; it does not
+prewarm the default working-tree path. Cache identity includes the profile,
+tree, cache directory, and graph-shaping ignore/include inputs. Run
+`entire graph index --help` when you need to control those details.
+
+## How much to trust
+
+Treat graph results as a map back to the code. Read the cited source and run the
+repository's tests or build before keeping a change. Static relationships can
+miss dynamic dispatch, reflection, generated code, and runtime wiring.
+
+Built-in analysis stays local. Installation obtains software over the network,
+`init-agents` writes the three files described above, and queries may write
+local caches. Check `entire graph doctor --json` to inspect the resolved
